claims.claim: Memory is shifting from crushing short-term numbers to long-term agreements with a floor and a ceiling, trading short-term upside for durability.
claims.prediction: Memory eps-surprise MAGNITUDE compresses faster than other layers, because contracted revenue does not surprise.

claims.threshold: < -2 supports; >= -2 refutes on current data

claims.verdict_detail: memory trend +9.7 vs others +3.1 -> relative +6.6

claims.claim: The investability screen (>=10 analysts AND >=$0.5B revenue) is too hard a gate and should be loosened or dropped.
claims.prediction: Loosening improves drawdown-adjusted return; dropping entirely is at least as good.
claims.why_it_matters: The screen decides the universe the signal orders. Too tight discards real names; too loose feeds the driver noise.
claims.metric: Calmar by (coverage floor, revenue floor), with thirds
claims.threshold: beats the incumbent on full-window Calmar AND 2 of 3 thirds
claims.action_if_supported: Adopt the winning screen.
claims.verdict_detail: PARTLY. The REVENUE half is pure cost and was dropped: it helps at every coverage level to remove it, and it blocked names for size not tradability (ASTS has 11 analysts and a $23B cap on $0.1B revenue). At $100k notional a 2% position is $2,000, so liquidity was never our binding constraint. COVERAGE is NOT pure cost: cov>=5 scores Calmar 8.22 vs 7.67 for NO screen (+0.55), which follows from the driver being EPS surprise — a name with no analysts has no consensus to beat. Adopted cov>=5 & no revenue gate: 8.22 vs 7.42 incumbent, beating it in the full window AND 2 of 3 thirds (11.5/9.2/15.7 vs 7.9/9.9/13.4).
claims.action_taken: MIN_ANALYST_COVERAGE 10->5, MIN_REVENUE_USD 5e8->0. Admits AAOI, ALAB, AMD, AXTI, CIEN, LITE, PENG, USAR.

claims.claim: valuation() drops names without a positive P/E, so compute_scores reads them as z_val 0.0 = AVERAGE valuation. That hard gate hits 21 of 96 names and 3 holdings at ranks 3/4/11 (INTC, SKHYNIX, SAMSUNG) on a leg weighted 1.0. It should be a fallback, not a gate.
claims.prediction: A fallback ladder (P/E where positive, else P/S) beats the hard gate.
claims.why_it_matters: A leg as heavily weighted as the EPS-surprise driver contributes nothing for three top-11 holdings, and the book cannot tell.
claims.test: VAL_METRIC=composite vs trailing_pe, full window + thirds
claims.metric: Calmar
claims.threshold: beats the gate on full-window Calmar AND 2 of 3 thirds
claims.action_if_supported: Set VAL_METRIC=composite.
claims.verdict_detail: THREE designs all fail, none winning a single third. trailing_pe hard gate 8.22 | composite scale-matched 6.40 | composite percentile+P/S 3.71 | percentile of P/E alone 3.55. TWO mechanisms: (1) ranking destroys the TAILS the leg runs on — z-scored raw P/E hammers ARM at 245x and rewards MU at 19x, while percentiles score the dearest name 1.0 whether it is 60x or 250x, costing 4.7 Calmar by itself; (2) imputation CONTAMINATES THE CROSS-SECTION — adding 20 fallback names moves the mean and sd the z-score is measured against, shifting z_val for all 75 names that never needed help. ARM entered the book without its own P/E changing. So z_val 0.0 is not a tolerated bug: 'I do not know' beats an imputed guess, because the guess pollutes the yardstick.
claims.action_taken: none; VAL_METRIC stays trailing_pe. The composite ladder ships in signals.valuation() but is off by default and available for re-testing with a different design.

claims.claim: A hard gate on non-positive trailing P/E makes no sense for high-growth stocks: a pre-profit hypergrowth name is dropped rather than valued. E/P (earnings yield) is the standard fix, continuous and monotone through zero, so no gate and no imputation are needed.
claims.prediction: VAL_METRIC=earnings_yield beats trailing_pe.
claims.why_it_matters: The valuation leg is weighted 1.0, as heavy as the EPS-surprise driver, and it is the ONLY leg negatively correlated with the rest (eps -0.16, thesis -0.15, mom -0.33, rev -0.13). It is the book's sole diversifier, so how it is expressed matters more than its weight.
claims.metric: Calmar
claims.threshold: beats trailing_pe on full-window Calmar AND 2 of 3 thirds
claims.action_if_supported: Set VAL_METRIC=earnings_yield.
claims.verdict_detail: E/P is far WORSE, and worse than having no valuation leg at all. trailing_pe 8.22 | leg OFF 5.49 | E/P w0.5 5.23 | E/P w1.0 2.23. The economics explain it: E/P sorts loss-making names as the most expensive and penalises them hard, but those are exactly the pre-profit hypergrowth names (CRWV, NBIS, IREN) this book wants to own on the AI-supply thesis. So the hard gate is not really 'we cannot value it' — functionally it is 'we decline to hold pre-profit AGAINST a name', which is the correct treatment for a growth book. The operator intuition was right about the economics and the current code accidentally implements the right answer. SEPARATELY this run refuted my own read that the leg was inert: removing it costs 2.73 Calmar (8.22 -> 5.49). Its -1% share of score VARIANCE is the signature of a NEGATIVELY-correlated diversifier, not of a dead leg. Variance share measures how much a leg moves the score, not whether it moves the right names at the rank-30 cut line.
claims.action_taken: none; VAL_METRIC stays trailing_pe. earnings_yield ships in signals.valuation() as an off-by-default option.

claims.claim: The valuation leg's measured 2.73 Calmar is partly foresight: panel_open's trailing_pe carries ONE value per symbol, so today's multiple is applied to every bar back to 2023-06-22, and a name that looks cheap today got there by earnings compounding faster than price.
claims.prediction: Rebuilding trailing P/E point-in-time from reported EPS keyed to report dates will cut the leg's contribution materially.
claims.why_it_matters: 2.5 of the score's 4.0 weight units (valuation 1.0, thesis 1.0, revisions 0.5) are static. If the valuation leg's value is foresight, so is part of every backtest run this week.
claims.metric: Calmar over the no-leg baseline
claims.threshold: PIT leg retains >70% of the static leg's margin over W_VAL=0
claims.action_if_supported: Keep W_VAL 1.0 on PIT data.
claims.verdict_detail: The leg is REAL, not foresight. Decomposed against the no-leg floor of 5.49: static-with-lookahead 8.22 (+2.73, NOT ACHIEVABLE LIVE), PIT with the old gate kept 7.73 (+2.24, the time-variation alone), PIT with adjusted EPS 8.31 (+2.82). 104% of the leg's value survives honest data, and PIT actually BEATS the lookahead version while cutting maxDD from -10.0% to -9.3%. Isolating the two axes: making the multiple time-varying is worth +2.24, and switching GAAP eps_ttm for analyst-basis reported EPS (which hands a positive multiple to the 15 names the old gate dropped as loss-making, INTC at rank 3 among them) adds a further +0.58. Against the only legitimate baseline (leg OFF, since a leg fed by unattainable data is not a real option) PIT wins the full window and all 3 thirds.
claims.action_taken: SHIPPED: USE_PIT_VALUATION now defaults ON. 98 symbols carry a rebuilt series; 33 (ETFs and index proxies, which have no company EPS) keep static values and are unaffected since the valuation leg does not score them.

claims.claim: The 42-name AI-supply thesis list is STATIC and was written in 2026, so replaying it from 2023 asks the book to already know which names became AI winners. CLAUDE.md's most load-bearing finding ('the edge IS the theme', W_THESIS=0 collapsing Sharpe 3.1 to 1.7) was measured on that basis and never re-run.
claims.prediction: The thesis leg performs like a hindsight winner-picker; its measured value is largely foresight.
claims.why_it_matters: Weight 1.0, equal to the EPS-surprise driver, and BINARY, so membership is worth a fixed ~2.0 score points against a rank-1-to-30 spread of ~3.3. It decides the book more than any other input.
claims.metric: Calmar, bounded between a random-list floor and a realised-winners ceiling
claims.threshold: REAL near the HINDSIGHT ceiling implies foresight; REAL near RANDOM implies no information
claims.action_if_supported: Cut W_THESIS and rebuild membership point-in-time.
claims.verdict_detail: REAL 5.48 BEATS the perfect-foresight ceiling of 4.66, so the leg cannot be winner-picking: a winner-picker scores at most what the actual winners score. RANDOM (1.11, sd 0.26, n=6) is BELOW the no-leg baseline of 1.49, which also kills the rival 'its value is structural, a binary flag perturbing selection near the rank-30 cut' hypothesis; a random list actively HURTS. So the leg's value is entirely informational. The likely mechanism: a realised-top-performers list is an ex-post selection of one-off pops with no common driver and does not cohere as a FACTOR, whereas an economically coherent supply-chain list co-moves and interacts with the EPS-surprise and momentum legs. Overlap between the two lists is 28 of 42 (67%), so the 14 names that differ carry the gap. NOTE the pre-registered bands assumed the ceiling was a ceiling and had no branch for REAL > HINDSIGHT; the script's printed verdict was wrong and the logic has been corrected. RESIDUAL, not addressed by this test: it shows the list is not selecting winners, but not that anyone would have chosen the AI-supply CATEGORY in 2023.
claims.action_taken: none; W_THESIS stays 1.0. 'The edge IS the theme' survives on stronger evidence than it was originally made on.

claims.claim: Momentum, thesis and revisions intercorrelate 0.45-0.56 and carry 2.0 of the 4.0 score weight, so half the score is substantially one factor. The nominal weights overstate what the confirmer legs independently contribute.
claims.prediction: Removing or decorrelating the redundant confirmer weight improves the book.
claims.why_it_matters: Two of five legs, 1.0 of 4.0 weight. Revisions is also the LAST lookahead leg (a dict with no date axis), so if it can go, the score becomes free of static-data contamination apart from thesis membership, which the hindsight bounding test already cleared.
claims.metric: Calmar
claims.threshold: beat live on full-window Calmar AND 2 of 3 thirds, then win a MAJORITY of neighbouring configs
claims.action_if_supported: Set W_MOM=0 and W_REV=0; score becomes eps + val + thesis at 1.0 each.
claims.verdict_detail: Dropping BOTH confirmers gives Calmar 6.49 vs 5.48 live and wins 6 of 6 neighbouring configs (TOP_K 20/30/40 x rebal 21/42), median +1.02, worst +0.13, never negative. An orthogonalised blend with confirmers at 0.25 independently lands at 6.46, so two routes to 'less confirmer weight' agree. THE 2x2 IS NON-ADDITIVE and remains unexplained: mom .5/rev .5 = 5.48, mom 0/rev .5 = 5.49 (momentum earns NOTHING), mom .5/rev 0 = 3.85 (removing revisions COSTS 1.63), mom 0/rev 0 = 6.49. The coherent reading is that MOMENTUM is actively harmful in this sample and revisions was partly offsetting it; remove momentum and revisions becomes redundant. CAVEAT: the win is concentrated in the later sub-periods (drop-both thirds 6.6/11.3/15.2 vs live 9.5/6.7/9.5), so it LOSES the first third, which is a regime-dependence flag. NOTE this contradicts the founding research ('EPS surprise ADDS to momentum, blend Sharpe 2.37 vs 1.87 mom-alone'), measured on the 34-name curated panel at TOP_K=8, a universe and config that no longer exist.
claims.action_taken: SHIPPED 2026-08-08: W_MOM=0.0 and W_REV=0.0 are the config defaults, both commented 'OFF since 2026-08-08'. The field previously read 'NOT YET SHIPPED - awaiting operator decision' and was stale for over a week, which is long enough for it to be read back as a live decision. The live score is eps + val + thesis at 1.0 each. RE-MEASURE the 2x2 if EODHD replaces the yfinance revisions source: the leg was NOT data-starved when tested (it reads data/revisions.json), so EODHD would be a better source rather than a first one, but the non-additive result (removing revisions ALONE costs 1.63 Calmar) is unexplained and a source change is exactly when to re-test it.

claims.claim: For recent IPOs, a meaningful drop against the IPO price or all-time high (~50%) marks entry into value territory and is a reason to go long.
claims.prediction: Deeper drawdown predicts higher forward return, especially for recent listings.
claims.why_it_matters: Fills a REAL gap: the valuation leg runs on trailing P/E and 15 universe names are loss-making, so they score z_val = 0.00 (AVERAGE, not unknown). Recent IPOs sit disproportionately in that bucket, so the book currently has NO cheapness input for exactly these names.
claims.metric: date-controlled excess forward return (63d) by drawdown bucket
claims.threshold: positive excess in a majority of sub-periods, not concentrated in a few names
claims.action_if_supported: Add a drawdown-based cheapness proxy for names without a positive P/E.
claims.verdict_detail: THE THRESHOLD IS REAL AND THE OPERATOR NAMED IT CORRECTLY, but the effect fails our own robustness bar. Date-controlled excess fwd63: drawdown <25% -0.15%, 25-50% -2.35% (the FALLING-KNIFE zone), >50% +4.55%, and RECENT listings >50% +10.90%. The relationship is NON-MONOTONIC, which is why a rank IC read it as noise or slightly wrong-signed (+0.057 for recent): a Spearman correlation across a U-shape sees nothing. THREE CHECKS WEAKEN IT: (1) sub-periods +9.01%, +11.61%, -4.32% — NEGATIVE in the most recent third, so it fails the 2-of-3 bar; (2) excess falls from +4.55% to +1.48% excluding just ASTS, CRDO and ALAB, so two thirds of it is three names; (3) SURVIVORSHIP is decisive — the panel is today's tradeable perps replayed backward, so any name that fell >50% and then delisted or collapsed is ABSENT ENTIRELY, and that bias lands hardest in precisely this bucket. The measured effect is an UPPER BOUND, not an estimate. Deep-drawdown value is exactly the hypothesis a survivorship-biased sample manufactures. || SENSITIVITY BOUND (2026-08-09) SETTLES IT WITHOUT NEW DATA. The bias has one shape — names that fell >50% then died are missing — so the question inverts to: how many missing failures would erase the edge? BREAKEVEN FAILURE RATES: all names >50% down (edge +4.55%) needs only 4.4% at a -100% delisting return, 7.1% at -60%, 13.5% at -30%. The strongest version, recent listings >50% down (edge +10.90%), needs 9.9% at -100% and 15.4% at -60%. Against a base rate of roughly 1 in 5 US IPOs from the 2020-21 cohort delisting or falling below $1 within three years — and failure CONCENTRATES in names already down >50%, so the conditional rate is higher still — every breakeven sits BELOW the plausible failure rate. The effect does not survive its own worst case. || MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED (2026-08-09). The Alpha Vantage key was already provisioned on the nickel Render service. LISTING_STATUS returns 9,412 delisted securities with IPO and delisting dates, plus a true point-in-time active universe. Survivorship-FREE cohort of US common stock that IPO'd 2020-01-01..2024-06-30: 2,646 still listed, 2,524 DELISTED, FAILURE RATE 48.8%, median life to delisting 680 days. Every breakeven in the sensitivity table is destroyed: the most generous was 26.8% (recent listings, -30% delisting return) against an actual 48.8%, and that is the UNCONDITIONAL rate, a lower bound on the rate conditional on being down >50%. NOTE MY OWN PRIOR WAS WRONG BY MORE THAN 2x — I estimated 'roughly 1 in 5' and reasoned from it; the truth is nearly 1 in 2. ONE HONEST COUNTER: AV 'delisted' includes acquisitions and mergers, which delist at a PREMIUM rather than a loss, so 48.8% overstates failures specifically. It does not overstate ABSENCE, which is what the survivorship bias is made of — an acquired name is just as missing from a yfinance-built panel. And even the -30% column, generous enough to cover soft landings, breaks at 26.8%.
claims.action_taken: REFUTED and closed. Not shipped. The AV listing data is kept at data/survivorship/ because it fixes something much larger than this one claim: it enables a point-in-time, survivorship-free universe, which is the caveat sitting on EVERY backtest number in this project.

claims.claim: EPS_SURPRISE_CAP=100 is not optimal: a different clip level, or an order-preserving transform, would improve the book.
claims.prediction: Some variant beats the shipping clip at 100% on risk-adjusted return.
claims.why_it_matters: A hard clip goes FLAT above the cap, so it does not merely bound the denominator artifact, it erases ordering inside the tail. Today AAOI (+300%), GIGADEV (+272%), AMZN (+215%), GOOGL (+214%) and AXTI (+164%) all score an identical z of 1.92, and their order in the book is then set entirely by the thesis and valuation legs. The cap is the single knob on the book's only driver leg.
claims.metric: paired block bootstrap dSharpe vs the shipping config (block 21, 2000 resamples), clip levels 50/150/300 + uncapped + log1p + rank
claims.threshold: 95% CI on dSharpe excludes zero (the bar THESIS_AS_GATE was held to)
claims.action_if_supported: Adopt the winning transform via cfg.EPS_TRANSFORM / EPS_SURPRISE_CAP.
claims.verdict_detail: NOTHING clears the bar: uncapped +0.218 CI [-0.256,+0.714], clip300 +0.158 [-0.150,+0.464], clip150 +0.134 [-0.075,+0.359], log1p +0.107 [-0.302,+0.518], clip50 +0.009. Every CI straddles zero, and log1p's evidence is WEAKER than the thesis gate we declined to ship on this same test (+0.232 [-0.232,+0.718]), so the default does not move -- switching would be fitting noise. TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING ANYWAY. (1) The shipping level is not defensible as OPTIMAL either: on point estimates clip 100 is the worst clip level above 50% (Sharpe 2.89 vs 3.03-3.13) and has the worst single sub-period (+2.24) of any variant, and its original 2026-06-16 justification (3.03->3.35) was measured on the old curated panel and does not replicate on the open universe. The right reading is that this knob is not resolvable on one AI-bull sample, not that 100 was chosen well. (2) rank percentile is the only variant measurably WORSE (-0.155, wins 21.8%), which says the MAGNITUDE of a beat carries signal and not just its order -- an argument against flattening the top at all. cfg.EPS_TRANSFORM=log1p ships as a one-flag switch if the tie-breaking argument is later judged to outweigh a null performance result.
claims.action_taken: EPS_TRANSFORM added (clip|log1p|rank), default UNCHANGED at clip 100.

claims.metric: paired block bootstrap dSharpe vs live (block 21, 2000 resamples); ONE-SIDED because every forward/growth field in the panel is one static value replayed to 2023-07-03, so lookahead flatters every arm — a LOSS is conclusive, a WIN is not
claims.threshold: 95% CI on dSharpe excludes zero
claims.claim: The valuation leg should price on FORWARD earnings instead of, or as well as, trailing P/E.
claims.prediction: Forward P/E ranks better than trailing because it covers more names, including the pre-profit ones trailing cannot price.
claims.why_it_matters: Coverage looked decisive: once the forward-estimates logger was fixed (42 -> 120 names), forward P/E prices 101 of 120 against trailing's 80, and it prices four of the seven holdings trailing cannot value at all — AAOI 33x, INTC 50x, SpaceX 69x, Cerebras 169x.
claims.action_if_supported: Set VAL_METRIC=fwd_pe or fwd_or_trailing.
claims.verdict_detail: BOTH forward arms are the two WORST of six and they lose while holding the lookahead advantage, which under the one-sided rule is conclusive. forward P/E dSharpe -0.299, wins 3.6%; fwd-else-trailing -0.238, wins 6.7%; Calmar 18.62 live -> 14.62 / 15.30 and drawdown deepens -13.1% -> -14.1%. The economics are the same mechanism that sank earnings-yield: pricing the pre-profit names at all means pricing them as EXPENSIVE (SpaceX 69x, Cerebras 169x), and penalising exactly the names the AI-supply thesis wants to own costs more than the extra coverage earns. Better coverage, worse book. Coverage is not the objective.
claims.action_taken: VAL_METRIC stays trailing_pe. fwd_pe and fwd_or_trailing ship in valuation() as tested-and-rejected options.

claims.metric: paired block bootstrap dSharpe vs live (block 21, 2000 resamples); ONE-SIDED because every forward/growth field in the panel is one static value replayed to 2023-07-03, so lookahead flatters every arm — a LOSS is conclusive, a WIN is not
claims.threshold: 95% CI on dSharpe excludes zero
claims.claim: Revenue growth deserves a score leg now that momentum is gone. It was dropped as 'redundant with momentum and noisier', and momentum has been at zero weight since 2026-08-08.
claims.prediction: Adding W_GROWTH.z(dispersion-damped forward revenue growth) improves the book.
claims.why_it_matters: Nothing in the live score promotes a name for growing. SpaceX carries $23B revenue at 52% gross margin and is held purely on EPS surprise plus the thesis. A factor discarded for overlapping a leg that no longer exists has not been tested against the book we run — the confirmer 2x2 already showed removing momentum changes what else is redundant.
claims.action_if_supported: Ship W_GROWTH at the winning weight.
claims.verdict_detail: Point estimates favour a SMALL weight with a sane dose-response: 0.25 -> dSharpe +0.107 (wins 78.0%), 0.50 -> +0.161 (79.1%), 1.00 -> -0.255 (21.2%), i.e. a little helps and a lot hurts. But no CI excludes zero (0.50 is [-0.249,+0.538]) and the test is ONE-SIDED: fwd_growth is a single value per symbol replayed back three years, so a win here may be nothing but lookahead. NOT shippable on this evidence. The honest route is already running for $0 — forward_estimates_logger now covers 120 names (it covered 42 until the PYTHONPATH fix on 2026-08-16) and the archive is 53 days deep, so this becomes answerable on point-in-time data in a few months. Re-test then, not before.
claims.action_taken: W_GROWTH added to signals, DEFAULT 0.0 (no-op). Re-test when the forward archive has PIT depth.

claims.claim: The tracked-fund 13F data should drive the book directly, not sit on a tab as context: either hold what the best funds hold, or add their flow as a score leg.
claims.prediction: A book selected on 13F data beats ours, and/or adding a 13F leg to the live score improves it.
claims.why_it_matters: 15 AI-frontier crossover funds, 26 quarters, the only external-capital input we have. It has been context-only by explicit decision since 2026-08-02, and that decision was never measured.
claims.test: research/smart_money_signal_test.py (bake-off) + research/smart_money_significance.py (paired block bootstrap + leg correlations)
claims.metric: standalone Sharpe vs the live book; paired block-bootstrap dSharpe for the overlay (block 21, 2000 resamples)
claims.threshold: standalone must beat the live book; overlay needs a 95% CI on dSharpe excluding zero AND leg correlation below 0.6 against every existing leg
claims.cadence: quarterly (new filings land ~45 days after quarter end; next round 2026-11-14)
claims.action_if_supported: Ship W_SMART=0.5 with SMART_METRIC=flow, SMART_UNCOVERED=neutral.
claims.verdict_detail: STANDALONE: REFUTED, clearly. Holding their names ranked their way loses to the live book on every variant (flow 1.43, best-ideas 1.18, conviction 0.10, consensus -0.28, vs LIVE 2.66), and the most obvious version, counting how many funds hold a name, is outright NEGATIVE. The ordering flow > best-ideas > conviction > consensus is the literature's, which is at least internally consistent. OVERLAY: the best candidate is flow at W_SMART=0.5 with uncovered names left out of the leg: Sharpe 2.66 -> 2.93 (dSharpe +0.278), Calmar 18.62 -> 19.04, better in ALL three sub-periods, with a sane dose-response (1.0 hurts, -0.075). It survives the redundancy check: max leg correlation 0.434 (momentum), and adding momentum itself HURTS (-0.423) while flow helps, so it is not momentum in a slow wrapper. But the bootstrap is t +1.53, 95% CI [-0.04, +0.68], wins 95.1% — the CI INCLUDES ZERO and the pre-registered bar was that it exclude zero. Eleven cells were tried, so one at 95% is roughly what chance produces. NOT SHIPPED: W_SMART stays 0.0. Two things make it the strongest candidate leg yet tested here: it is the FIRST tested on genuinely point-in-time data (the panel is keyed on filing dates, median 44-day lag), so unlike the forward-P/E and growth tests a win is not flattered by construction; and 'no tracked fund holds it' carries no information (the negative reading scores +0.115 against neutral's +0.278). STRUCTURAL CEILING regardless of significance: quarterly filings give four updates a year against a 21-day rebalance, so this can only ever be a slow tilt. PACE + UNIVERSE, added 2026-08-16 after the operator asked about the rate of accumulation and the position's share of their book. THEIR UNIVERSE IS A WORSE HUNTING GROUND THAN OURS: gating to the names they hold and ranking with OUR OWN live score scores 2.13 against 2.66, so restricting to their names costs 0.53 Sharpe before any 13F ranking is applied. Their ranking then loses again on top of that (flow-only 1.43 on the same universe). PACE DOES NOT ADD OVER DIRECTION: persistence (streak of consecutive accumulating quarters) +0.144 and log-magnitude (flow_log, winsorized at 5x) +0.107, both WEAKER than the plainly bounded flow at +0.278. The informative part of a 13F change is WHETHER they are adding, not how hard — bounding magnitude helps rather than hurts. And the share of their book is the worst reading of all: conviction LEVEL adds +0.030 (nothing) and conviction CHANGE is NEGATIVE at -0.185, which fits, since pct_aum moves with price and with the fund's other positions. Sixteen cells have now been tried, so the multiple-comparisons problem is WORSE than when the 95.1% was recorded: one cell at 95% out of sixteen is what noise produces. Verdict unchanged.
claims.action_taken: W_SMART=0.0 (inert, registered). Re-test after the 2026-11-14 Q3 filing round extends the PIT archive.

note: CLAIMS REGISTER. Every external claim we have taken seriously enough to test, with the testable prediction it implies, the test that decides it, and the standing verdict. Run by research/claims_register.py. The point is that a refuted claim STAYS refuted without re-arguing it, an inconclusive one gets re-tested on a cadence instead of being forgotten, and a verdict that FLIPS raises an alert. Nothing here changes a weight; each entry records what we would do if the verdict changed, so that decision is made in advance rather than in the moment.
